 Oral Judgment

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
for short) has been filed by the claimants being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated
11.12.2018 passed by the I Addl. District Judge and Mact, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal')
in Mvc No.1083/2017.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 02.05.2017 at about 8.45 p.m.,
when the deceased Manjunatha was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-06/EG-6791 from Holavanahalli to go to Akkirampura through Honnaranahalli Gowribidanur road, at that time, a Boloro vehicle bearing registration No.KA-06/D-2261 which was being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the deceased.

As a result of the Narasamma vs Radha M on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174932311/
2 aforesaid accident, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

sentences.text: 3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1,
and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
On behalf of respondents, neither any one witness was examined nor got exhibited documents.
The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia

, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.14,96,400/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, this appeal has been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants raised the following contentions:
NC: 2024:KHC:32245 i)
Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was approximately aged about 25 years at the time of the accident and had a monthly income of Rs.13,000/- as a Mason.
However, the assessment of income of the deceased at Rs.9,500/- by the Tribunal is unjustified and erroneous.
ii) Secondly, there are four claimants and they are the legal representatives of the deceased.
In view of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to file an application seeking compensation.
In lieu of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the claimants are depending upon the income of the deceased.
The Tribunal instead of deducting 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses of the deceased erred in deducting 1/4th of the income.

iii) Thirdly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ NC: 2024:KHC:32245 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
Narasamma vs Radha M on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174932311/
3 v) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.

sentences.text: With the above submissions, learned counsel for the appellants sought to allow the appeal.

7. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits as follows:
i) Firstly, although the claimants claim that the deceased was earning Rs.13,000/-
per month, they failed to substantiate their claim with supporting documents.
Consequently, the Tribunal has correctly assessed the income of the deceased notionally.

ii) Secondly, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, the legal representatives are entitled to compensation only if it is proved that they are depending upon the NC: 2024:KHC:32245 income of the deceased.
In the course of examination of PW1, there is an admission that claimant Nos. 3 and 4 are married and are living separately with husbands.
The claimant No.2 is living separately and the claimant No.1 is the only dependent of the deceased.
The Tribunal has rightly deducted 50% of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.
iii) Thirdly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
With the above submissions, learned counsel for the Insurance Company sought to dismiss the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal and the original records.
NC: 2024:KHC:32245 9.
It is not in dispute that Manjunath died in the road traffic accident occurred on 02.05.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. The claimants claim that deceased was earning Rs.13,000/- per month, but failed to produce supporting documents to substantiate their claim.
In the absence of proof of income, the notional income has to be assessed.
According to the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, for accidents occurred in the year 2017, the notional income of the deceased shall be taken at Rs.11,000/- p.m.

To the aforesaid income, 40% has to be added on account of future prospects in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157].

the monthly income comes to Rs.15,400/-.
The claimants are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, all the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to file an application for compensation.

Only the legal representatives who have NC:

sentences.text: In the case on hand, claimant No.1 is the mother of the deceased.
She has been examined as PW1.
In her chief-examination she has deposed that the claimants are entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Even in the cross-examination she has not admitted that the claimants were not depending upon the income of the deceased.
It is the specific case of the claimants that the deceased was taking care of his mother, brother and sisters and they were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Even in the ration card - Ex.P9, the name of claimants is also shown along with the name of PW1.

Considering the evidence of PW1 and Ex.P9, I am of the opinion that 1/3rd of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards personal expenses and remaining amount, i.e., Rs.10,267/- has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 25 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '18'.

Thus, the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32245 claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.22,17,672/- (Rs.10,267*12*18)
on account of 'loss of dependency'.
11.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.

12. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant No.1, mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

13. Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 22,17,672  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of filial consortium 40,000

In the result, the following order is passed:
Narasamma vs Radha M on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174932311/
5 ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

sentences.text: (ii) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

(iii) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.22,87,672/- as against Rs.14,96,400/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

(v) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
(vi) The apportionment, deposit and release of amount shall be made in accordance with the terms of the award of the Tribunal.
